# Task Slices: ICS file import

## Dependency graph

```text
Wave 1:  T1 Native atomic batch persistence     T4 Browser import API
                 |                                      |
Wave 2:  T2 ICS conversion coordinator           T5 Calendar import UI
                 |
Wave 3:  T3 Authenticated HTTP endpoint
                 \                                      /
Wave 4:                  T6 Integrated E2E + docs
```

Executable dependency form:

```text
T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T6
T4 -> T5 -------> T6
```

T1 and T4 may run in parallel because their write scopes are disjoint and their
shared contract is fixed in the approved architecture and program design. T2 and
T5 may also run in parallel after their respective prerequisites. T3 stays on
the backend chain because it consumes T2's error and summary types. T6 begins
only when both tracks are complete.

## T1 — Atomically create a native event batch

- Outcome: `EventService` can create multiple ordinary or recurring native
  events and their occurrence exceptions as one authorized, audited transaction.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `backend/src/event.rs`; initial batch-persistence cases in
  `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add the approved `EventCreateBatch`, item, exception, recurrence-key,
  and result types; implement `EventService::create_batch`; reuse existing event
  validation, recurrence validation, authorization, audit, CalDAV change, and
  notification-replanner helpers; add focused service tests for atomic rollback,
  exception persistence, side-effect counts, and native editability.
- Out of scope: ICS parsing or UID grouping, HTTP routes, parser error mapping,
  rate-limit classification, frontend work.
- Acceptance: A valid mixed batch commits all top-level events and exceptions;
  invalid input or a database failure commits none; authorization is checked as
  `CreateEvent`; every top-level row has one create audit and CalDAV change;
  imported-style rows have no external mapping and remain editable; notification
  replanning occurs only after commit.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_batch`
- Handoff: Stable batch input/result types and proven transactional semantics for
  the ICS coordinator; record exact type names if implementation-required Rust
  adjustments preserve the approved meanings.

## T2 — Convert an ICS file into a native event batch

- Outcome: Bounded valid ICS bytes become native event batches with preserved
  standalone, all-day, timed, recurrence-exclusion, and detached-override
  semantics.
- Depends on: T1
- Scope: new `backend/src/ics_import.rs`, `backend/src/lib.rs`, recurrence and
  parser-limit cases in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportService`, import constants, summary, and errors; invoke
  the existing parser with the 1,000-event policy; normalize status and timing;
  group components by UID; attach `EXDATE` and `RECURRENCE-ID` values; reject
  orphan, mismatched, conflicting, unknown-status, malformed, duplicate, and
  over-limit input before persistence; delegate once to `create_batch`; export
  the module.
- Out of scope: HTTP body/media-type handling, route mounting, rate limiting,
  browser API or UI, changes to external-feed ingestion or the generic parser.
- Acceptance: Timed and all-day standalone events import with correct fields;
  a recurring master stores deletions and replacements under the correct keys;
  every semantic or parser failure maps to the approved error category and
  leaves all persistence tables unchanged; re-import creates another editable
  native copy; summary counts top-level events separately from exceptions.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_service`
- Handoff: Callable `IcsImportService::import`, stable summary/error contract,
  content-free failure categories, and tested constants for T3.

## T3 — Expose the authenticated, limited import endpoint

- Outcome: Authorized callers can POST raw `text/calendar` bytes and receive the
  approved summary or stable safe error codes through the production router.
- Depends on: T2
- Scope: `backend/src/http.rs`, `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs`, HTTP and role cases
  in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Mount and implement `POST
  /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics`; verify media type and non-empty
  body; call `IcsImportService`; map errors; emit content-free structured timing
  logs; classify the route as Standard write rate; add authenticated role,
  response-envelope, media-type, 1 MiB limit, and classifier tests.
- Out of scope: service conversion rules, database schema, frontend behavior,
  application-state or router-builder signature expansion.
- Acceptance: Owner, manager, and editor receive 201 for valid input; viewer,
  free/busy viewer, and unrelated caller receive non-enumerating 404; malformed
  and limit failures expose only their stable codes; incorrect media type and
  empty input are 400; oversized input is 413; the route is Standard-rate
  limited; logs contain no calendar content, UID, filename, title, description,
  or location.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked ics_import`
- Handoff: Final backend endpoint contract and complete integration-test evidence
  for the browser and E2E packets.

## T4 — Add the typed browser import API

- Outcome: Frontend callers can upload a `File` as raw calendar content and
  receive typed counts or a safe typed failure code.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts`, `frontend/src/calendar/api.test.ts`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportSummary`, error-code type,
  `IcsImportApiError`, and `importIcs`; send the `File` body with the approved
  media type; parse only `error.code`; fall back safely for malformed or unknown
  error responses; add focused request/response tests.
- Out of scope: Dialog state, card permissions, file prevalidation, styling,
  backend implementation.
- Acceptance: The client uses the exact approved route, method, content type, and
  unmodified `File` body; successful counts are returned; recognized codes are
  typed; unknown bodies never surface server-provided text.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- api.test.ts`
- Handoff: Stable `importIcs` function, summary, and safe error class for T5.

## T5 — Deliver the accessible calendar import flow

- Outcome: Owners, managers, and editors can select, validate, upload, and
  acknowledge an ICS import from an active calendar card.
- Depends on: T4
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.tsx`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.css`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Changes: Add the event-creation permission helper and per-card import action;
  implement the import dialog and its file-size/extension validation, pending,
  success, safe-error, Escape, focus, and access-change behavior; style it using
  existing calendar-dialog conventions; add all approved component tests.
- Out of scope: Backend changes, event-list refresh mechanics, calendar creation
  during import, preview or event selection, E2E fixture.
- Acceptance: Only active detail-access owner/manager/editor cards show Import;
  editors gain no management controls; invalid local files make no request;
  a valid file submits once; all pending controls are safe; success shows the
  returned count until acknowledgement; stable failure codes show actionable
  copy without backend text; access denial refreshes calendars; Escape and close
  restore focus to the correct card.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Handoff: Completed visible flow and selectors/accessibility names needed by the
  E2E packet.

## T6 — Prove the integrated user journey and document it

- Outcome: A browser-level test proves a real ICS file becomes editable native
  events, and public project documentation describes the new capability.
- Depends on: T3, T5
- Scope: new `e2e/support/import.ics`,
  `e2e/tests/desktop-mvp.spec.ts`, `README.md`, final integrated verification
- Changes: Add the deterministic two-event fixture; drive the visible import
  dialog; assert the success count; verify both events through the API as native
  and writable; update the README feature list and API overview; run focused and
  full relevant checks and fix only regressions caused by this feature.
- Out of scope: Expanding import behavior, deduplication, provider connections,
  external-feed changes, unrelated cleanup or pre-existing failures.
- Acceptance: The desktop E2E flow imports one timed and one all-day event and
  proves they are not external/read-only; README clearly distinguishes one-time
  import from feed subscription; backend and frontend suites, formatting,
  linting, typechecking, build, and the focused E2E test pass together.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir e2e test -- desktop-mvp.spec.ts --project=desktop`
- Handoff: Final test evidence, any environment-specific E2E notes, and confirmation
  that all six packet acceptance conditions pass together.

## Slice-fit review

### T1

- One outcome and one seam: native batch persistence.
- Binary proof: commit-all/rollback-all plus side-effect assertions.
- Lands working without exposing an unused route.

### T2

- One outcome and one uncertain boundary: normalized ICS to native batch.
- Parser and recurrence policy are local to the new coordinator.
- Binary proof: semantic conversion and zero-write failure cases.

### T3

- One outcome and one seam: authenticated HTTP exposure.
- Consumes stable T2 interfaces; makes no product decisions.
- Binary proof: status, error code, access matrix, body limit, and rate tier.

### T4

- One outcome and one seam: typed browser transport.
- Fully disjoint from backend writes and independently testable.
- Binary proof: exact request and safe response mapping.

### T5

- One user flow: calendar-card import dialog.
- Uses stable T4 interface and existing dialog conventions.
- Binary proof: permission, validation, pending, result, error, and focus tests.

### T6

- One outcome: integrated proof and user-facing documentation.
- Contains no new implementation behavior; it verifies both completed tracks.
- Binary proof: browser journey plus full relevant checks.

All packets pass the slice-fit test. None crosses more than one uncertain seam,
each has one primary verification path, and shared-file work is sequential within
its track.
